Voat is Reddit's subcommunity structure without Reddit's culture or administration. Hopefully the good without the bad, and so far that's been my experience here. You get the odd hostile comment here or there, but that's part of free speech. Parts of Voat feel like the Canada of the internet; people know how to disagree respectfully, which keeps this place from becoming a shouting match or an echo chamber.

Also with Reddit you don't know what's going on under the hood; there's vote fuzzing, shadowbans, and no modlog. On Voat there's an open modlog for each subverse that tracks all moderator activity to keep things as transparent and predictable as possible. Voat has an anti-censorship culture, so there's less tolerance of what the community perceives as unfair moderator activity, which is a good thing as long as we don't go overboard with witch hunts. The admins have a hands-off approach and don't interfere with lawful content. Instead of having admin curating content for you, you as a user have the ability to block subverses you don't want to see.
